The mountains here in state. The atmosphere there is incomparable to anything else I've visited. Being surrounded by nature: the trees, creeks and rivers, etc. compared to monotonous sidewalks, concrete, bricks, and asphalt.

I'd like to live there someday; alone. Ride my bicycle everywhere and become part of a small, close-knit community in a small town. Just thinking about it makes me feel comfortable.
Locally, I'm quite fond of a park bench under some cherry trees. It's a 40 minute walk there, and then I sit there writing on my laptop until the battery runs out.

There's this one park near my house that I've been going to for as long as I can remember. I play basketball there most days, but whenever I feel really happy or sad or confused or pissed off I lie down at the top of the hill at the centre of the park. I usually do this at night so I can look at the stars. That hill has got me through the best and worst of times.

Ruidoso and Cloudcroft, New Mexico. Cloudcroft is 9000 ft above sea level, only a few hours' drive away, and the air feels so clean and crisp, the sky seems bluer, it's always way cooler than where I live. It's really cool to rent a cabin for a few days and just get away from everything. Great place to go.

The other place (which I wish I could visit now) is the Japanese Botanical Gardens inside the Fort Worth Botanical Gardens in Fort Worth, Texas. It's like another world and everything is always beautiful and landscaped and you can't hear the noises of the city, just the sound of the waterfalls and the breeze through the maples. I miss that place.

Haven't been many places in terms of holidays, so I'll go with what I like in my city.

The beach. Just go chill out on the beach and listen to the waves. Ain't nothing better.

There's one particular stretch of beach where no one ever goes, so it's always just me and the waves. So good.
